Alger, 21 août 2026 (Algeria Tech) — Dan: Algiers, August 21, 2026 (Algeria Tech) — In a strong symbolic momentum, celebrated on the occasion of Moudjahid Day, Oran is hosting a major industrial first: the commissioning of a smartphone assembly plant, the fruit of a bold partnership between Algerian start-up Smart Technologie Innovation (STI) and Chinese giant Vivo. With an initial capacity of two thousand daily units and a stated ambition of six thousand, this seven-thousand-square-meter infrastructure, which is set to employ up to six hundred direct workers and more than one thousand two hundred indirect ones, embodies much more than a simple technology transfer — it crystallizes a national strategy of industrial resilience and digital sovereignty.
Une inauguration sous le signe de l'exem: An inauguration under the sign of industrial excellence
L'enceinte de l'usine Smart Technologie: The Smart Technologie Innovation (STI) plant site, located in the Oran industrial zone, was officially inaugurated this Thursday, August 20, 2026, in the presence of the wali of the wilaya, Ibrahim Ouchane, as part of the Moudjahid Day celebrations. This timing is not insignificant: it symbolizes the anchoring of this initiative in a broader vision of economic and social development, where the technology industry becomes a lever for structural transformation. Driven by a 100% Algerian company, this plant marks a decisive step in the diversification of the national industrial fabric, long dependent on imports of electronic goods.
L'établissement, qui s'étend sur sept mi: The facility, which spans seven thousand square meters, represents a substantial investment in the real economy. From its launch, the plant employs two hundred workers, seventy percent of whom are job seekers registered with the National Employment Agency (ANEM). A statistic that resonates particularly in a wilaya where youth unemployment easily exceeds twenty percent. But beyond the numbers, it is the company's philosophy that catches the attention: an integrated approach combining production, training, and professional integration.
Un modèle vertueux : formation, emploi e: A virtuous model: training, employment, and technological sovereignty
L'un des piliers de ce projet réside dan: One of the pillars of this project lies in its coordination with the Algerian vocational training system. Djilali Boukhelaf, STI's communications officer, emphasized the pedagogical innovation represented by the creation of a specialized professional qualification certificate in smartphone manufacturing and assembly — a first in Algeria. This curriculum, co-constructed with stakeholders from the Vocational Training and Education sector, trains young people in skills directly aligned with the plant's operational needs. The commitment is clear: to recruit beneficiaries upon completion of their training, thus transforming unemployment into employability.
Cette démarche s'inscrit dans une logiqu: This approach is part of a virtuous circularity logic, where industry feeds training and vice versa. It also addresses a strategic imperative: reducing the country's dependence on smartphone imports, the cost of which exceeds several billion dollars annually. According to the latest data from the National Office of Statistics (ONS), mobile phone imports reached nearly three billion dollars in 2025, an amount that weighs heavily on Algeria's trade balance. By focusing on progressive local integration — with the ultimate goal of manufacturing all feasible components locally — STI and its partner Vivo aim to shift this expenditure item towards productive investment.
Transfert de technologie et sécurité num: Technology transfer and digital security: the two invisible pillars
Le partenariat avec Vivo ne se limite pa: The partnership with Vivo is not limited to assembling smartphones under license. It includes an ambitious technological component, centered on the transfer of know-how and the improvement of product quality. Specifically, the agreement provides for the integration of software directly within the Algerian factory, an approach aimed at strengthening the security of digital products marketed locally. In a context where cyber threats and risks of intrusive surveillance are multiplying, this initiative takes on a geopolitical dimension: it aligns with the orientations of the Algerian state regarding digital sovereignty.
Par ailleurs, la création future d'un se: Furthermore, the future creation of a dedicated R&D service, in collaboration with Algerian universities and research centers, heralds a new era for local innovation. The objective? To develop software tailored to the specific needs of Algerian users, while training a generation of engineers and technicians capable of competing with international standards. An agreement in principle has already been signed with several institutions, including the University of Science and Technology of Oran (USTO) and the National Higher School of Computer Science (ESI), to lay the foundations for this collaboration.
Oran, nouveau hub technologique de l'Afr: Oran, North Africa's new tech hub?
L'implantation de cette usine à Oran n'e: The establishment of this factory in Oran is no coincidence. The wilaya, the country's third-largest city and second-largest economic hub after Algiers, benefits from an already well-structured industrial ecosystem, with an abundant supply of qualified labor and suitable logistical infrastructure. It notably hosts the port of Arzew, one of the most important in the country, which facilitates the supply of imported components and the export of finished products.
Cette initiative s'inscrit dans une tend: This initiative is part of a broader trend observable in the North African region, where countries like Morocco (with the Renault plant in Tangier) or Egypt (with Transsion's smartphone assembly project) are betting on the high-tech industry to boost their growth. However, Algeria stands out for its desire to combine local integration and technological sovereignty, two axes rarely associated with such determination in the African landscape.
Analyse et enjeux : vers un écosystème i: Analysis and stakes: towards an integrated ecosystem?
L'arrivée de STI à Oran soulève une ques: The arrival of STI in Oran raises a crucial question: can this plant catalyze a local industrial ecosystem around electronics? Several clues point to a positive answer. First, the stated desire to gradually increase the local integration rate, with the ultimate goal of full production of components achievable in Algeria. This strategy could attract other industry players, thereby creating a ripple effect.
Ensuite, l'accent mis sur la R&D ouvre l: Next, the focus on R&D opens the door to collaborations with Algerian startups specializing in fintechs, software solutions, or IoT (Internet of Things). Ultimately, this ecosystem could enable Algeria to cease being a mere consumer market for international giants and become a full-fledged player in the global value chain.
However, major challenges remain. The first concerns the competitiveness of locally assembled products against massive imports from Asia or Europe. The second touches on training: how to guarantee a sufficient talent pool to feed a rapidly expanding industry, not to mention the skills shortages already threatening other sectors? Finally, the issue of environmental sustainability cannot be avoided: a plant of this scale will quickly have to comply with international standards in electronic waste management and energy efficiency.
Contexte et perspectives : l'Algérie sur: Context and outlook: Algeria on the path to Industry 4.0
Cette usine s'inscrit dans le cadre du P: This plant is part of the Development Plan for the Electronic and Digital Industries Sector, launched in 2024 by the Ministry of Industry and Mines. This plan aims to raise the share of the electronics industry in GDP to five percent by 2030, compared to less than two percent today. To achieve this, the state is relying on incentive measures, such as tax exemptions for local businesses and investment subsidies.
À moyen terme, plusieurs indicateurs doi: In the medium term, several indicators must be monitored to assess the impact of this project. First, the plant's actual ability to reach its target of six thousand smartphones per day within two to three years. Next, the local integration rate, which will need to be measured transparently to avoid empty promises. Finally, the emergence of local subcontractors capable of providing components or auxiliary services to the STI plant.
Par ailleurs, l'expérience oranaise pour: Furthermore, the Oran experience could inspire other wilayas. Rumors are already circulating about similar projects in Annaba, Constantine, or Sétif, where underutilized industrial zones could host new high-tech infrastructure. If these initiatives materialize, Algeria could become a key player in the electronics sector in Africa, much like Morocco in the automotive industry.
